ownership_reason: Only the gold decides whether a banner (the header or the footer) is printed. Hop 1 prints the usage statement and documents that each print method of the formatter writes at least one complete line; hops 1 to 4 each document that the header and the footer are handed on as they are given; hop 4 only places the header banner, the options and the footer banner in that order, calling the gold once per banner on separate lines. The gold's javadoc promises the lines of the banner wrapped to the width; an empty banner has no lines, yet the variant hands it to the formatter and an empty line is printed. No one-line change elsewhere restores the help consistently with the documentation on the path: the trigger passes an empty header and an empty footer, so a pre-filter of one banner at hop 4 leaves the other empty line; a trim of the values at hops 1-3 keeps "" as ""; replacing the values at hops 1-4 contradicts their 'handed on as they are given'; and making HelpFormatter.printWrapped write nothing for an empty text contradicts hop 1's documented property of the formatter's print methods, which printUsage and printOptions keep (printOptions writes an empty line even for an empty Options, testHeaderStartingWithLineSeparator). The convention that text without content counts as absent is pinned outside the gold by production code doing the same step on other text of the help: Option.hasArgName (an empty arg name is no arg name), HelpFormatter.appendOption ('non blank argname': an empty arg name adds no <...> to the usage clause) and HelpFormatter.renderOptions (an empty arg name adds no <...> to the option's entry), with testPrintOptionWithEmptyArgNameUsage passing; the help's layout without blank lines between its parts is pinned by testOptionWithoutShortFormat2 and testHelpWithLongOptSeparator, and a banner with text is printed as given (testHeaderStartingWithLineSeparator).
